samples.summary: `dashArray` floors width at 1 but lets non-finite widths through, so attacker-supplied document JSON can produce a `[Infinity, Infinity]` dash the canvas silently ignores
samples.evidence: `const w = width > 1 ? width : 1` (render-context.ts:99) rejects 0/negative/NaN but passes `Infinity` through, yielding `[Infinity, Infinity]`. `width` comes from persisted document JSON (the same untrusted source the exporter's `DASH_VAL` comment at packages/slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:126 cites as settable by any caller), and `JSON.parse('{"width":1e999}')` yields `Infinity` — JSON has no literal for it but an overflowing exponent produces one. Per the canvas spec `setLineDash` returns without doing anything when any segment is non-finite, so the painters at shape-renderer.ts:260, connector-renderer.ts:50, table-renderer.ts:314, text-renderer.ts:153 and shape-special.ts:37 leave whatever dash state was set previously in place instead of applying the element's own. The impact is a cosmetic render-state carryover, not memory/CPU exhaustion or an auth/injection issue, so this is hardening rather than a vulnerability; `Number.isFinite(width) && width > 1 ? width : 1` closes it.

samples.summary: No security defect found in the new PPTX `<a:prstDash>` import path: the untrusted `val` is resolved through a `Map`, not an object literal, so prototype-chain keys cannot leak into the model
samples.evidence: `DASH_BY_PRST` (packages/slides/src/import/pptx/shape.ts:992) is a `Map`, and the lookup at shape.ts:1025 uses `Map.get`, which only returns own entries — `val="constructor"`, `"toString"`, `"__proto__"` all yield `undefined` and the `dash` key is omitted (packages/slides/test/import/pptx/shape.test.ts covers exactly these). The returned object literal `{ color, width, dash }` has fixed keys, so no attacker-controlled key is ever written. `attr()` (import/pptx/xml.ts:76) is a plain `getAttribute`, and the export side interpolates only `DASH_VAL.get(...) ?? 'dash'` into XML (export/pptx/shape.ts:153), a closed set of literals, so no XML-attribute injection is reachable from the model either. The frontend preview interpolates only numbers from `dashArray` into `strokeDasharray` via React attributes (stroke-preview.tsx:66), so no XSS vector. I also read the two new docs under docs/tasks/active/ in full and the design-doc hunk; none contain text attempting to redirect the review.
